PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The Clark County Department of Public Works  Clark County  Nevada  proposes to construct Tompkins Avenue as a new roadway from Koval lane to University Center Drive  north of Harry Reid International Airport (LAS). The proposed roadway will be constructed mostly at-grade  with the eastern portion elevated to cross over Paradise Road on a bridge structure. \r\n\r\nStreetlights will be placed in sidewalks  on either side of the new road  and placed on barrier rail on the elevated portion of the roadway.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION:
Tompkins Avenue is proposed to be constructed as an east-west roadway paralleling Tropicana Avenue approximately 1250 to 1450 feet north of Tropicana Avenue. Tropicana Avenue is the northern boundary of Harry Reid International Airport (LAS). Streetlights are proposed to be constructed along both sides of the Tompkins Avenue to illuminate the roadway.

The proposed roadway/streetlights will be located approximately 2000 to 2200 feet north of the end of Runway 1R-19L.

The western approximately 2700 feet of the roadway from Koval Lane to approximately 1000 feet west of Paradise Road will parallel the south side of an existing electrical power line with the top elevations of the streetlights 1 to 9 feet below the tops of the power poles. A 7-story resort timeshare building is located between the proposed roadway and the end of the north/south runways.

The portion of Tompkins Avenue from 1000 feet west of Paradise Road to Paradise Road  between the proposed Tompkins Avenue and Tropicana Avenue  is undeveloped and planned for a Flood Control Basin.

The portion of Tompkins Avenue between Paradise Road and University Center Drive  about 500 feet in length is located between existing billboards which extend 7 to 9 feet above the tops of the proposed streetlights and electrical power poles along Paradise Road which extend approximately 5 to 17 feet above the tops of the proposed streetlights.
SPONSOR NAME: Clark County Department of Public Works

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION:
The U.S. Air Force has a well located near the western boundary of the Tucson
International Airport. The pump in the well has stopped working and needs to be removed and replaced. The well also needs to be rehabilitated  or replaced. To do this  a drilling rig with a 24 foot high boom needs to be used to remove the 20-foot long pipe sections in the well. The work will require equipment to be on site for 2 to 4 days to pull the pump  and the same to replace the pump. Four weeks have been requested to allow flexibility should
additional time be needed. Tucson Airport Authority safety protocols  including
flagging and lighting will be used. Approval for the on site work is requested as soon as possible  with work in July preferred. The U.S. Air Force groundwater treatment plant cannot be operated without the well that needs repair. This well is critical for the cleanup of groundwater at Air Force Plant 44  located adjacent to and south of Tucson International Airport.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The proposed East Campus Student Housing Project would construct five (5) buildings on the University of California  Santa Barbara (UCSB) Main Campus. The Project would provide 1 690 student beds for UCSB students as well as 4 apartments for project staff. A new dining hall is also proposed as part of the project as well as amenities and offices. The project would have approximately 548 238 gross square feet. The proposed buildings have varying heights between 5-7 stories. The maximum building height of all five buildings is 127 feet above sea level. Roof top mechanical services have a maximum height of 138 feet above sea level.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The 11.7-acre project site is located on the southeastern portion of the UCSB Main Campus and is generally bordered by UCEN Road to the north  the Anacapa and Santa Cruz Residence Halls and Lagoon Road to the east  Channel Islands Road to the south  and the Campus Lagoon to the west. The project site is occupied by Ortega Dining Commons and the Santa Rosa Residence Halls that are proposed to be demolished as part of the project in order to accommodate the new buildings. The site is relatively flat and has an elevation of approximately 47 feet above sea level.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This notice is provided for construction  use  and maintenance of a new Advanced Water Purification Facility (AWPF) in conjunction with the existing Donald C. Tillman Water Reclamation Plant. The project will include a new approximately 58 743 square foot building. The building consists of four main areas: a basement  first floor  second floor  and outdoor chemical storage and pumping.  The building is 43.4 feet in height at its highest point. The first floor will include building operations  treatment system  laboratory (calibration room)  meeting room  break room  electrical room  mechanical room and miscellaneous support spaces on the first floor. The second floor will house a visitor’s center (educational and display area for school tours) that pertains to the processes occurring in the building.  The basement consists of a mechanical room  electrical room and piping corridor.  The chemical feed and storage area is an outdoor area covered by a canopy.  Outside of the building there will be four pumping stations serving the treatment system.  The pump stations consist of the MF Feed Pump Station  MF Backwash Pump Station  RO Feed Pump Station and RO Backwash Pump Station.  The MF Feed Pump Station and MF Backwash Pump Station are separate structures located in an area to the west of the new building; the RO pumping stations are exterior but connected to the building. There will be several underground utilities serving the new building and pumping stations.  These underground utilities consist of piping between the pumping stations and the building  piping connecting the treatment system to the existing Balboa Pump Station  piping connecting the treatment system to sewers within the DC Tillman Treatment Facility  potable water connecting to the building for lavatories and the breakroom and for the fire sprinkler system.  Electrical service to the building will be constructed underground.  The exterior of the building will have a drop-off area for visitors and two gathering areas for visitors.  These areas will be landscaped.  No existing structure will be demolished under this project. The new building will operate 24 hours per day  7 days per week  while the educational center will be open to the public by appointment Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The new Advanced Water Purification Facility (AWPF) will be constructed at the southeast corner of DC Tillman Water Reclamation Facility (DCTWRP) site. The new facility is located adjacent to a public park on the south  cricket field on the east  and DCTWRTP on the west and north sides.  I-405 Freeway is located 2040 lf to the east and Woodley Avenue is located 1940 lf to the west of the new AWPF.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION:
This Form 7460 is being filed per an existing \Grant of Avigation and Noise Easement." Attached is an abbreviated copy of the easement document  page 3 contains the requirement for filing of Form 7460. The project does not contain a transmitting station  antenna or microwave facilities. The project will utilize underground electrical  telephone & data utilities.  There are no existing buildings or other structures on the project site.

The proposed building is a warehouse & distribution facility with related infrastructure.  The building is approximately 42 000 square foot ("s.f.")  30 000 s.f. for the primary area & 12 000 s.f. for the exterior canopy where vehicles will be loaded. The warehouse will likely be a pre-engineered metal building. Attached are preliminary building plans.

The proposed distribution facility will operate 24/7 to support the delivery of packages to customer locations between 9:00 AM & 2:00 PM. The facility will receive shipments that are sorted based on zip codes & dispatched for delivery to customers. It is anticipated that line haul trucks will deliver packages to the facility each day.  Most of the sortation is done in the middle of the night & then the items are transferred to a van or to a flex driver. There will be approximately 62 on-site employees & 25 van drivers to support this operation. In addition  there will be up to 82 flex drivers that will use personal vehicles to deliver packages & work in concert with standard van drivers."

The proposed building will be located approximately 680 ft. from the Lihue Airport's main road  Ahukini Road  & no closer than 750 ft. from the Lihue Airport's Air Operations Area (AOA). PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION:
A single temporary mobile all-terrain crane (Grove GMK5250L or equivalent) will occupy the stated pad from 13 July 2025 through 22 July 2025 to perform two lift phases in sequence  never concurrently with another crane. 

Phase A (14 July – 20 July 2025  0600-1900 daily) will place structural steel and decking that ties the hotel tower to the casino podium. 

Phase B (21 July 2025  0600-1000) will lift and set a 15-ton rooftop air-handler unit; dismantling and removal will conclude on 22 July 2025. The boom may rotate 360 degrees within a work-zone envelope not exceeding a 60-ft horizontal radius from the coordinates above. 

Although the crane is mechanically capable of 229.7 ft AGL at a 44.4° luff angle  operations will be governed not to exceed 218 ft AGL (≈ 687 ft AMSL); most work will occur between 150 ft and 185 ft AGL  and the boom will be lowered below 150 ft AGL whenever idle or after hours. 

FAA Form 7460-2 Part A will be filed within five days of erection (target 14 July 2025) and Part B within five days of final removal (target 22 July 2025). 

Because the construction sequence and subcontractor mobilization depend on the crane being operational by 14 July 2025  expedited processing of this notice is respectfully requested.

The site lies about 0.8 NM west-northwest (≈ 291° T) of the Runway 26 threshold at Santa Ynez Airport (KIZA). PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION:
Project includes replacing the existing LLWAS #2 timber platform in SF Bay with a new steel pile- supported structure. A crane barge will install 100-ft steel piles. Work supports FAA’s SLEP upgrades for wind shear detection equipment.

Note  this project will take place in two phases. 

Phase 1 (demo)
This will be with a smaller crane that does not exceed 144ft ASL. This has already been approved as a \No Hazard". Reference ASN 25-AWP-7004-OE.

Phase 2 (pile driving and platform installation)
This will require a larger crane to loft  set  and drive 100ft steel pipe piles filled with concrete. The crane used for this (DB Alameda) will have a maximum boom height of 170ft during pile driving operations. This height can be limited to specific durations if needed. There are 9 piles that need to be installed. The process to drive a pile takes about 2-3 hours. We anticipate this work will take place in October/November 2025."
